objective: Build a national outdoor decision-intelligence network that turns authoritative public data into explainable, place-specific decisions without weakening Michigan canonicals, source truth, or search quality.

phase2.principle: Deepen decision usefulness and source transparency before expanding URL count.

smokeAirQuality.reason: AirNow developer access and NASA FIRMS MAP_KEY are required for the intended authoritative implementation. Do not ship a weaker fake-live substitute.

fallCurrentObservations.source: USA-NPN Nature's Notebook Status & Intensity data, Colored leaves phenophase 498
fallCurrentObservations.rule: Recent nearby individual-plant observations may be shown as current ground evidence, but they never become a landscape percent-peak estimate and never mathematically alter the historical timing model.
fallCurrentObservations.failureMode: The core historical timing and NWS weather answer renders without waiting for this optional source; failure remains isolated to the observation panel.
fallCurrentObservations.coverage: 75-mile radius, 21-day lookback, conflicting status records excluded

phase3.principle: Make the five tools behave like one decision platform before adding another product family or location-page surface.

alerts.rule: Do not label saved places, local state, or passive UI as alerts. Ship alerts only when the system can actually deliver a future notification and preserve source/freshness semantics.

measurement.rule: Measure national location-resolution success, tool transitions, saved-place use, and hub input health before expanding indexable location surfaces.
measurement.privacy: Never send raw city/ZIP text, display names, coordinates, postal codes, or saved-place names as analytics event properties.
measurement.expansionGate: Measurement provides evidence for the location admission contract; it does not by itself grant indexability.

location.rule: Manual city/ZIP remains the default. Device location runs only after an explicit user tap, is rounded to 0.001 degrees before the server request, uses POST rather than a coordinate URL, and never enters analytics.
location.continuity: After reverse geocoding, cross-tool links carry the resolved place query rather than latitude/longitude.

placeToolbar.shareRule: Shared national-tool links may carry the resolved city/state query but never latitude/longitude. Canonical URLs remain the base tool routes.
placeToolbar.analyticsRule: Save, switch, and share events may record action/method only; place names, ZIPs, and coordinates remain excluded.

comparison.rule: Compare the five core source-backed signals plus coastal context where real source coverage exists, without producing an overall winner, universal score, or safety determination.
comparison.measurement: A comparison event may record signal count only; selected place identities remain excluded from analytics.
comparison.indexability: Comparison is local UI state on the canonical hub and creates no new indexable URL.

usgs.rule: No production runtime request or future index generation may depend on waterservices.usgs.gov.

verification.productionSmoke: 43/43 public-origin checks passed after merge on 2026-09-02

searchOpportunityMatrix.rule: A score of 80 is necessary but not sufficient; canonical, source, truth and thin-page hard gates still apply.

phase0.scope: Existing five national products and source lifecycle hardening, including USGS migration.

phase1.scope: Decision Desk, saved places, cross-tool continuity, comparison, privacy-safe analytics and independent degradation.

phase2.gate: AIRNOW_API_KEY and FIRMS_MAP_KEY plus supported-interface verification remain required.

coastalProduct.canonicalIntent: U.S. beach and coastal conditions today by location
hardRules: Official NWS High or Moderate beach risk is never downgraded by buoy or tide context.
No universal beach, swimming or boating safety score.
Missing source data remains unavailable rather than neutral or favorable.
NDBC station distance is visible because an offshore station is not exact beach truth.
CO-OPS tide predictions remain predictions and never masquerade as observed water level.
Michigan users are handed to the deeper Michigan Beach Report instead of cloning that canonical.
Source proximity alone does not qualify a location as coastal; location admission must pass before NDBC or CO-OPS context is shown.
Portland, Oregon and other inland locations must return not-applicable even if distant coastal or tidal sources fall within the broader discovery radius.
coastalProduct.dashboardBehavior: Optional sixth card only after coastal location admission passes and real coastal source coverage exists; inland places retain the five core cards.

locationAdmission.basis: Nearest applicable NOAA/NWS Marine Beach Forecast Summary area
locationAdmission.rule: A location must be within 25 miles of an applicable NWS beach-forecast area before buoy or tide context can be shown. Source proximity alone does not qualify a location as coastal.
locationAdmission.failClosed: If NWS beach applicability cannot be verified, the tool returns coverage-unverified and suppresses buoy/tide context rather than guessing.

locationResolution.primary: U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb for city/state and ZIP
locationResolution.fallback: OpenStreetMap Nominatim for flexible queries and reverse geocoding
locationResolution.rule: A transient failure from one geocoding dependency must not strand ordinary U.S. city/state or ZIP tool entry.

snowProduct.canonicalIntent: U.S. snowpack, snow depth, SWE and snowmelt conditions by location
sourceFamilies: NOAA/NOHRSC provisional snow depth and SWE station observations

geography.rule: Source proximity is not local pack truth. Stations outside 60 miles may be shown only as regional context and cannot drive a local pack-phase conclusion.

decisionOrder: local 48-hour NWS temperature and precipitation wording
hardRules: NOHRSC station observations remain labeled unofficial and provisional.
No nearby SNOTEL station is never interpreted as no snow.
Missing measured snowpack remains unavailable rather than zero or favorable.
Melt pressure is a transparent site-derived interpretation and never masquerades as a NOAA, NWS or NRCS snowmelt forecast.
Snow does not infer avalanche danger, groomed-trail condition, road access, ice safety or a universal recreation safety score.
Snowmelt context does not predict river response; Rivers retains measured flow and official forecast intent.
No Snow candidate authorizes generated city, ZIP or resort location pages.
snowProduct.dashboardBehavior: Optional Snow card only when current measured pack is present or the local NWS forecast contains a snow signal. Otherwise the five core cards remain, with Coastal separately optional where applicable.
snowProduct.cannibalizationBoundary: National Snow owns measured snowpack plus weather-driven melt/refreeze context. Michigan XC tools retain trail/grooming/ski-planning intent; Rivers retains flow and official flood/river forecast intent.

productionSmoke.invariant: A local pack-phase conclusion requires measured pack within 60 miles; otherwise melt pressure remains not-evaluated.

whiteChristmasProduct.canonicalIntent: Will I have a White Christmas? Current-year probability by U.S. location
whiteChristmasProduct.definition: At least 1 inch of snow on the ground on December 25.
sourceFamilies: NOAA/NWS CPC monthly and seasonal outlooks

model.output: Rounded 5-point probability estimate with visible confidence and factor contributions
model.earlySeason: 1991-2020 station history dominates; CPC can only nudge the prior
model.snowpackWindow: Current measured snowpack begins influencing inside 45 days and only within 60 miles
model.shortRangeWindow: NWS Christmas-period forecast becomes a major factor only inside 8 days
model.precisionRule: Never display a one-point probability; round to five points to avoid false precision.

hardRules: The percentage is site-derived synthesis and must never be labeled an official NOAA/NWS White Christmas forecast.
Historical baseline requires at least 25 valid December 25 snow-depth observations in 1991-2020.
White Christmas uses the NOAA one-inch snow-depth definition, not snowfall during Christmas Day.
CPC seasonal/monthly categories may only nudge the historical prior because they are broad-period outlooks.
Snowpack outside 60 miles cannot alter the local White Christmas estimate.
Short-range NWS weather can dominate only after December 25 enters normal forecast range.
No guarantee or certainty language at any probability.
No raw place, ZIP or coordinates in analytics.

longTail.blockedPattern: Mass city, ZIP, county or state doorway generation
longTail.futureAdmission: Require distinct query intent, primary-source depth, internal network fit and measurable search opportunity before any new supporting URL.
